assumptions.assumption: A fixed word list finds the kind of claim a statement makes. It does not read meaning: negations ('there will be no ceasefire'), quotations of others and mixed statements are misread.
assumptions.test: Hand-label 100 statements from the first month against the classes; report precision and recall per class on the method page before any rule uses them.

assumptions.assumption: Activity in the same country within 72 hours of a calm claim is worth a look. It is not evidence that the claim was false: the activity may be by another party, unrelated, routine for that place, or the claim may be about somewhere else in that country.
assumptions.test: Stated on the page, in the feed note and in every candidate-gap summary. RO-IND-1 stays proposed and moves no tier.

assumptions.assumption: The suite bus (COP's today.geojson) carries the other programs' current anomalies and warnings, so a missing pair means the sensors saw nothing, not that the bus was down.
assumptions.test: The suite lane's health and problems list say when the bus or a direct feed failed; the page shows say-do as not read then. Check pairs against COP's own map for a week.

assumptions.assumption: Countries named in a statement are what it is about. A statement can name a country in passing (a visit, a list of attendees) and miss one it is about (the 'occupied territories').
assumptions.test: GOV.UK's own world-location tags are used first where they exist; country names, demonyms and capitals are matched in the title and kept text. Review unmatched statements in the first month.

assumptions.assumption: Each publisher's English feed carries all its statements. The Kremlin's English site lags and omits some Russian-language items; GOV.UK search is limited to three departments; the EEAS page is read two pages deep.
assumptions.test: Stated on the method page. Counts per run are in the lanes block.
